confirmedRace.before: start and becameActive await bootstrap with isWorking=true and automaticOperation=nil. Async enteredBackground sees no automatic worker to cancel; old bootstrap resumes and creates a new ungranted background automatic worker. A rapid current activeB was also dropped by becameActive early isWorking return.
confirmedRace.notClaimed: This race is source-proven. It is not a reproduction of a specific device failure, and the fix does not establish Apple authorization, successful installation or unattended renewal.

behavior: One existing Owner holds ignored O(1) scene phase/epoch facts. The App records the actual initial scene synchronously and captures that epoch for .task; scene-change handlers record before enqueueing any async cleanup/activation. Late Tasks cannot announce a new active phase.

Each active epoch reserves at most one activation request across startup and becameActive. Latest activeB waits on actual Owner idle continuations while A bootstraps or another Owner operation drains. It rechecks its own phase/epoch/cancellation after every relevant await; obsolete A cannot adopt B authority. No sleeps, timer polling, new owner, store or worker pipeline are added.

Enabling captures its foreground epoch before the persistence await and only admits a worker if still active/current/uncancelled afterward. Manual run uses the same foreground admission. Local opt-in publication is not rolled back merely because the scene changed.

The system BGProcessingTask bridge calls an explicit background-granted entry into the same existing worker. Scene cleanup cancels only foreground-origin workers; it still waits for their actual cancellation/drain and preserves pairing cancellation. Expiration cancellation reaches the common worker and final result exactly as before.

An obsolete background cleanup checks its epoch before touching work and again after awaiting foreground drain, preventing it from cancelling a later active epoch. Close invalidates foreground admissions before its existing cancellation/drain.

Three DEBUG-only observation hooks provide signals after real Session bootstrap, after actual idle-wait registration, and inside the actual automatic worker. They replace no Session operation, use no real credential/phone, and are absent from Release.

newCases.fact: Hold the real startup bootstrap, record background, drain scene cleanup, release bootstrap; actual Session publishes unconfigured status and no automatic worker is created.

Hold A bootstrap, move background then activeB, wait for actual B idle-registration signal before release, submit duplicate B; require two real bootstrap observations and exactly one actual B worker, then reject delayed old-background cleanup.

At background, perform actual automatically:false startup; hold the common background-granted worker, invoke scene cleanup, release; actual disabled Session result succeeds and foreground manual entry is refused.
Cancel the real foreground activation while its bootstrap observation is held; release, drain the caller and assert no new automatic worker.

regressions.existingCallerMigration: All five existing becameActive callers now record inactive then active and pass that exact token, including two repeated material refresh pairs and the shared-handoff reopen. All five existing automatic Owner start callers explicitly record inactive/active and pass the token. The new background automatically:false start remains background. Existing positive full-renewal, manual App execution and material revalidation assertions/definitions remain intact.
